item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Marcos lifted major website blocks, ended red-tagging in practice, curbed libel or regulatory pressure on critical outlets, or introduced a concrete legal shield for independent journalists and media owners. The strongest positives are mostly rhetorical or state-internal anti-disinformation measures. The strongest negatives are independent assessments showing the underlying coercive media environment persisted.","evidence":[{"title":"Marcos publicly pledged a free and safe environment for journalists","publisher":"Presidential Communications Office","date":"April 15, 2024","url":"https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-declares-free-safe-environment-for-journalists-under-bagong-pilipinas/","summary":"Marcos said critical press is preferable to compliant press and framed journalist safety as part of Bagong Pilipinas. This is pro-media rhetoric, but it is intent rather than proof of practice.","question_ids":["4B.6","4B.3","4B.5"]},{"title":"The government responded to a manipulated deepfake with investigation and possible legal action rather than a broad censorship sweep","publisher":"Presidential Communications Office","date":"April 26, 2024","url":"https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-vows-legal-action-vs-deep-fake-video-creators-spreaders/","summary":"The state treated the deepfake as a misinformation problem, involving DICT and the NSC and pursuing legal remedies. That is a protective response against disinformation, though not a guarantee of press freedom.","question_ids":["4B.6","4B.5","4B.3"]},{"title":"The administration expanded eFOI access and kept a media-literacy/disinformation campaign in place","publisher":"Philippine News Agency","date":"January 18, 2024","url":"https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217036","summary":"This supports a limited transparency posture and some public-information access. It is helpful evidence for information access, but it is modest and not a substitute for independent media protections.","question_ids":["4B.6","4B.4"]},{"title":"PCO said it would designate fact-check officers in state media and denied a red-tagging policy","publisher":"Presidential Communications Office","date":"September 9, 2024","url":"https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pco-to-designate-fact-check-officers-in-state-media-to-fight-fake-news/","summary":"The state took a formal anti-disinformation step inside its own media apparatus. That is a real positive, but it is mostly internal state-media governance, not protection of independent outlets from pressure.","question_ids":["4B.6","4B.5"]},{"title":"Marcos urged journalists to help fight fake news while affirming a free press","publisher":"Philippine News Agency","date":"August 27, 2024","url":"https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1232026","summary":"Marcos publicly framed journalism as central to informed citizenship and said the government valued a free press. Again, this is supportive rhetoric, not a demonstrated change in media conditions.","question_ids":["4B.6","4B.3"]},{"title":"Independent reporting still found persistent press-freedom problems under Marcos","publisher":"Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism","date":"June 17, 2024","url":"https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines","summary":"The report says Marcos was more media-friendly than Duterte, but press-freedom concerns persisted, including red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats to journalists. This is strong negative evidence against a clean protection finding.","question_ids":["4B.6","4B.3","4B.5"]},{"title":"Freedom House said online information remained manipulated, including pro-Marcos disinformation","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-net/2024","summary":"Freedom House reported that online sources were manipulated by government and other actors, and that pro-Marcos disinformation networks helped rebrand the Marcos family. It also noted that site blocks from the Duterte era remained in place.","question_ids":["4B.6","4B.3","4B.5"]},{"title":"Freedom House said critical media still faced regulatory and law-enforcement pressure","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024","summary":"The report says media outlets faced intense political pressure, including regulatory and law-enforcement tools used against critical coverage, and that red-tagging continued under Marcos. This weighs heavily against a full-protection finding.","question_ids":["4B.6","4B.3","4B.5"]},{"title":"Human Rights Watch reported red-tagging of activists and critics under Marcos","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"January 11, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk","summary":"HRW said red-tagging under Marcos put leftist activists and critics at serious risk. That is direct evidence of a hostile information and intimidation environment.","question_ids":["4B.6","4B.3","4B.5"]},{"title":"Human Rights Watch reported threats against union leaders by officials and security actors","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"September 25, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders","summary":"HRW found officials and police or military members repeatedly threatened union leaders by accusing them of communist links. That is coercive pressure on civil society, not protection of independent information space.","question_ids":["4B.6","4B.3","4B.5"]},{"title":"Amnesty said Marcos-era actors weaponized misinformation and anti-terror framing","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"October 14, 2024","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/8574/2024/en/","summary":"Amnesty described a fear climate in which activists, journalists, teachers, and others were vilified through red-tagging and misinformation. This is strong negative evidence, though not limited to direct presidential orders.","question_ids":["4B.6","4B.3","4B.5"]},{"title":"The U.S. State Department report still listed media restrictions and threats","publisher":"U.S. Department of State via ecoi.net","date":"2024","url":"https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128580.html","summary":"The report says credible abuses including media restrictions and threats to labor activists remained. That supports the conclusion that the environment was not cleanly protective of independent media.","question_ids":["4B.6","4B.3","4B.5"]}]}
